label: First-source uniqueness through nature and real determinations
summary: The existing Q11 and root-multiplication derivations require incommunicability of the individuating basis, its agreement with nature, and common nature. Simpleness, esse–essence identity and first-being priority yield absence of represented limiting principles. They leave common nature open. De ente uses a separate relation of sharing nature and an explicit multiplication inventory. The real-thisness alternative requires strict purity, possession of every pure determination and a sufficient individuation principle. Existing omission models isolate bare numerical difference and a non-pure individuating determination. The #2016 model separates unique selected root from uniqueness among necessary beings.
blocker: Determine whether two unreceived whole natures could differ without a receiver, limiting determination or priority relation. Independently test whether numerical difference needs a real determination in the selected first-source domain.
